Japan Recovers After 2021 Yen Crisis Rattled Economy and Major Firms

TOKYO, June 27 – Japan’s economy has stabilized after the unprecedented currency crisis of 2021, which saw the yen plunge to record lows and caused widespread disruptions across the country’s industries, including utilities provider Tokyo Gas Co Ltd.

The crisis began in early 2021 when international investors lost confidence in the yen amid concerns about Japan’s mounting public debt and sluggish vaccine rollout. The currency tumbled rapidly, falling from around 105 yen per U.S. dollar in January to a low of 156 yen by late April, triggering a sharp rise in import costs and fueling inflation not seen in decades.

The currency collapse sent shockwaves through Japanese businesses. Energy companies, heavily reliant on imported fuel, were among the hardest hit. Tokyo Gas Co Ltd, Japan’s largest city gas supplier, faced soaring costs for liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports, forcing it to issue a rare profit warning in May 2021.

“We had no choice but to adjust our financial outlook as LNG prices jumped and the yen depreciated sharply,” said Tokyo Gas Co Ltd spokesperson Keiko Tanaka at the time. “The sudden increase in costs put significant strain on our operations, and we took immediate steps to secure supply and manage expenses.”

The Japan Business Federation estimated that the currency slide added more than ¥3 trillion (about $27 billion at the time) to annual import bills nationwide. The government responded with a series of emergency measures, including currency market interventions and a ¥10 trillion relief package for affected industries.

While the crisis ignited fears of a broader recession, the Bank of Japan kept monetary policy ultra-loose and coordinated with other central banks to stabilize foreign exchange markets. “Swift action was necessary to prevent a downward spiral in consumer confidence and business investment,” said Hiroshi Nakamura, chief economist at the Japan Economic Research Institute.

By late 2021, the yen had partially recovered, settling around 124 yen to the dollar, and inflationary pressures began to subside. Most sectors gradually returned to normal operations, and Tokyo Gas Co Ltd reported a rebound in profits in early 2022.

Today, economic activity in Japan is no longer disrupted, but analysts caution that the 2021 yen crisis underscored the country’s vulnerability to sudden currency movements and reliance on imported energy. “The episode was a wake-up call,” said Nakamura. “Japan must strengthen financial resilience to guard against future shocks.”
